prompt: How fast does light travel through a vacuum?
blurb: Light covers about 300,000 km every second — fast enough to lap the Earth 7.5 times in the time it takes to blink.

prompt: What is the average distance from the Earth to the Moon?
blurb: You could line up every planet in the solar system in the gap between Earth and the Moon and still have room to spare.

prompt: What is the diameter of the Sun?
blurb: About 1.3 million Earths would fit inside the Sun.

prompt: How long is a single day on Mars?
blurb: A Martian day (a 'sol') is just 40 minutes longer than ours — one of the solar system's friendlier coincidences for future settlers.

prompt: How fast does the International Space Station orbit the Earth?
blurb: At roughly 28,000 km/h the ISS circles the planet once every 90 minutes — 16 sunrises a day for the crew.

prompt: How far is the Earth from the Sun?
blurb: This distance — about 150 million km — is called one Astronomical Unit, the solar system's standard measuring stick.

prompt: How old is the universe?
blurb: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old — roughly three times older than the Earth.

prompt: Roughly how many neurons are in the human brain?
blurb: Around 86 billion neurons — close to the number of stars in the Milky Way.

prompt: How many bones are in the adult human body?
blurb: Babies are born with about 300 bones; many fuse together as we grow, leaving 206.

prompt: How many times does a human heart beat in a single day?
blurb: About 100,000 beats a day, pushing roughly 7,500 litres of blood around your body.

prompt: If you stretched out all the DNA in a single human cell, how long would it be?
blurb: About 2 metres per cell. Uncoil every cell in your body and the DNA would stretch to the Sun and back dozens of times.

prompt: How many breaths does a person take in a day?
blurb: Around 20,000 breaths a day — most of which you never notice taking.

prompt: How long does a red blood cell live?
blurb: About 120 days, after which it's recycled. Your bone marrow makes over 2 million new ones every second.

prompt: About how many taste buds does a person have?
blurb: Around 10,000, and they're replaced every week or two — which is why a burned tongue recovers so quickly.

prompt: What is the average normal human body temperature?
blurb: The classic 37°C figure dates to 1851; modern studies suggest the true average has drifted slightly lower.

prompt: How fast does human scalp hair grow per month?
blurb: About 1.25 cm a month — roughly 15 cm a year, or the length of a new pencil.

prompt: How many times does a person blink per minute, on average?
blurb: About 15–20 times a minute — but that rate drops sharply when you're staring at a screen.

prompt: How many chromosomes does a typical human cell contain?
blurb: 46 — arranged in 23 pairs. A potato, for comparison, has 48.

prompt: How many minutes per night does an average adult spend dreaming?
blurb: Around two hours a night across several REM cycles — most of which you'll forget within minutes of waking.

prompt: How tall is Mount Everest above sea level?
blurb: At 8,849 m, its peak sits in the 'death zone' where there's too little oxygen to sustain human life for long.

prompt: How deep is the deepest point in the ocean (the Mariana Trench)?
blurb: Drop Everest into the Challenger Deep and its summit would still be over 2 km underwater.

prompt: How long is the Amazon River?
blurb: About 6,400 km — it carries more water than the next seven largest rivers combined.

prompt: How long is the Nile River?
blurb: At about 6,650 km the Nile flows through eleven countries on its way to the Mediterranean.

prompt: How large is the Sahara Desert?
blurb: At 9.2 million km² the Sahara is nearly the size of the entire United States.

prompt: How hot does the air in a lightning bolt get?
blurb: A lightning channel briefly reaches about 30,000°C — five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.

prompt: How tall is Hyperion, the tallest known living tree?
blurb: This coast redwood tops 116 m — taller than the Statue of Liberty. Its exact location is kept secret to protect it.

prompt: How deep is the Grand Canyon at its deepest?
blurb: About 1.8 km deep, carved by the Colorado River over an estimated 5–6 million years.

prompt: How tall is the Horseshoe Falls at Niagara?
blurb: Only about 57 m tall, but more than 2,800 tonnes of water pour over it every second.

prompt: What is the Earth's circumference around the equator?
blurb: About 40,075 km. The metre was originally defined so that this distance would be almost exactly 40 million of them.

prompt: How deep is Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake?
blurb: At 1,642 m deep, Baikal holds about a fifth of all the unfrozen fresh water on Earth.

prompt: How long is the Great Barrier Reef?
blurb: Stretching about 2,300 km, it's the only living structure visible from space.

prompt: How tall is the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building?
blurb: At 828 m it's so tall you can watch the sunset from the base, then ride to the top and watch it set again.

prompt: How long is the Great Wall of China, counting all its branches?
blurb: A 2012 survey put the total at about 21,000 km — and no, it isn't actually visible to the naked eye from space.

prompt: How many member states does the United Nations have?
blurb: 193 members, the newest being South Sudan, which joined in 2011.

prompt: How many countries are there in Africa?
blurb: 54 sovereign countries — more than any other continent.

prompt: What is the highest air temperature ever reliably recorded on Earth (Death Valley, 1913)?
blurb: 56.7°C, hot enough to cook an egg on the ground — people have tried.

prompt: In what year did humans first land on the Moon?
blurb: Apollo 11 touched down in July 1969 with less computing power than a modern pocket calculator.

prompt: In what year did World War II end?
blurb: 1945 — the deadliest conflict in human history, drawing in more than 30 countries.

prompt: Around what year did Gutenberg complete his printing press?
blurb: Around 1440. Within 50 years, print shops had spread to over 100 European cities.

prompt: In what year did the French Revolution begin?
blurb: The storming of the Bastille in 1789 is still marked every July 14th as France's national day.

prompt: In what year was the US Declaration of Independence adopted?
blurb: Adopted on July 4, 1776 — though most delegates actually signed it weeks later in August.

prompt: In what year was the Eiffel Tower completed?
blurb: Built for the 1889 World's Fair and meant to be torn down after 20 years — it survived because it made a great radio antenna.

prompt: In what year was the Roman Colosseum completed (AD)?
blurb: Completed around 80 AD, it could hold an estimated 50,000 spectators.

prompt: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
blurb: The wall came down in November 1989 after standing for 28 years.

prompt: In what year were the first modern Olympic Games held?
blurb: Athens, 1896 — with 241 athletes from 14 nations, all of them men.

prompt: Around what year did Leonardo da Vinci begin painting the Mona Lisa?
blurb: He started around 1503 and reportedly kept tinkering with it for years, carrying it with him until his death.

prompt: In what year did the Beatles form?
blurb: Formed in Liverpool in 1960, they'd broken up within a decade — yet still define 1960s pop.

prompt: In what year was the first Academy Awards ceremony held?
blurb: The first Oscars in 1929 lasted just 15 minutes.

prompt: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
blurb: 88 keys — 52 white and 36 black — spanning a range wider than any orchestral instrument.

prompt: How many interlocking rings are in the Olympic symbol?
blurb: Five rings, one for each inhabited continent, in colours chosen so that every national flag of 1913 contained at least one of them.

prompt: In what year did Tim Berners-Lee propose the World Wide Web?
blurb: His 1989 proposal was famously described by his boss as 'vague but exciting.'

prompt: In what year was the first iPhone released?
blurb: The 2007 original had no app store, no copy-paste, and couldn't record video.

prompt: In what year was YouTube founded?
blurb: Founded in 2005; the very first video, 'Me at the zoo', is 19 seconds long.

prompt: In what year was the first networked email sent?
blurb: Ray Tomlinson sent it in 1971 and chose the @ symbol to separate the user from the machine.

prompt: In what year was the first SMS text message sent?
blurb: The first text, sent in 1992, simply read 'Merry Christmas.'

prompt: Roughly how many people use the internet worldwide today?
blurb: Around 5.4 billion people — about two-thirds of everyone alive.

prompt: Roughly how many articles are in the English Wikipedia?
blurb: Nearly 7 million articles, all written and edited by volunteers.

prompt: How fast does sound travel through air at room temperature?
blurb: About 343 m/s — which is why you see distant lightning well before you hear the thunder.

prompt: At what temperature does gold melt?
blurb: 1,064°C. Gold is so unreactive that most of the gold ever mined still exists today.

prompt: At what temperature does water freeze, in Fahrenheit?
blurb: 32°F. Fahrenheit set 0° using a freezing brine solution, which is why water's freezing point lands on such an odd number.

prompt: At what temperature does water boil at the summit of Everest?
blurb: Only about 71°C, because the air pressure up there is a third of what it is at sea level — which makes a decent cup of tea nearly impossible.

prompt: How many elements are on the periodic table?
blurb: 118 confirmed elements, the heaviest of which exist for only fractions of a second before decaying.

prompt: How old is the Earth?
blurb: About 4.5 billion years — and life appeared within its first billion.

prompt: How much does an adult blue whale weigh?
blurb: Up to about 150 tonnes — the largest animal ever known to have lived, heavier than the biggest dinosaurs.

prompt: What is a cheetah's top sprinting speed?
blurb: Around 110 km/h, but only in bursts of 20–30 seconds before it overheats.

prompt: What is a hummingbird's heart rate in flight?
blurb: Up to about 1,200 beats a minute — roughly 20 a second.

prompt: How long is an elephant's pregnancy?
blurb: About 22 months, the longest of any land animal.

prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
blurb: Three: two pump blood to the gills, one to the rest of the body — and the main heart stops beating when it swims, which is why octopuses prefer to crawl.

prompt: How tall is an adult male giraffe?
blurb: Up to about 5.5 m, yet it has exactly the same number of neck vertebrae as you do: seven.

prompt: How many times per second does a honeybee beat its wings?
blurb: About 230 times a second — that rapid beat is exactly what you hear as the buzz.

prompt: How many calories are in a medium banana?
blurb: About 105 — and bananas are naturally slightly radioactive thanks to their potassium.

prompt: How much caffeine is in a typical cup of brewed coffee?
blurb: Around 95 mg, though it varies wildly with the bean, roast and brew.

prompt: How many calories are in a McDonald's Big Mac?
blurb: About 563 — the sandwich has been used as an informal index to compare prices between countries.

prompt: How many teaspoons of sugar are in a standard can of Coca-Cola?
blurb: About 10 teaspoons — more than the daily added-sugar limit many health bodies recommend.

prompt: Around what year was the Margherita pizza reportedly created?
blurb: Legend says it was made in 1889 for Queen Margherita, its toppings matching the three colours of the Italian flag.

prompt: How long is a marathon?
blurb: 42.195 km exactly — the odd figure was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics so the race could finish in front of the royal box.

prompt: What is a typical length for a professional soccer pitch?
blurb: About 105 m. Unusually for a major sport, the rules allow the pitch size to vary from stadium to stadium.

prompt: How high is the rim of a basketball hoop?
blurb: Exactly 3.05 m (10 feet) — the same height James Naismith used when he invented the game in 1891.

prompt: Roughly how many walking steps are in one mile?
blurb: About 2,000, which is where the popular '10,000 steps a day' target gets its roughly-5-mile feel.

prompt: Roughly how many words does an average adult English speaker know?
blurb: Estimates land around 20,000–35,000 — a tiny slice of the half a million-plus words in the language.

prompt: How many keys are on a standard full-size QWERTY keyboard?
blurb: Typically 104 on a US full-size layout, including the number pad.

prompt: How many times does a human heart beat in an average lifetime?
blurb: Around 2.5 billion beats. Curiously, most mammals get roughly the same lifetime total, whether they live fast or slow.
